summary: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 14:31 - v3.7.1 (commit d999201, pushed). ROOT CAUSE of 'only 2 frames, rest black, tab stalled at 2min': abandoning a seek does not cancel it. Both capture loops set video.currentTime, waited for seeked OR a 1500ms timeout, then drew. When seeks exceed 1500ms (remote/HLS/large files) the loop gives up and assigns currentTime again, which SUPERSEDES the still-pending seek - so the element perpetually re-seeks, never settles, the position barely advances (hence a 34-min video stuck near 2min), and nearly every drawImage captures a stale or empty decoder. Occasionally one seek wins the race = the 1-2 good frames. Compounded by seeked firing before the decoder paints. FIX: new src/lib/frame-capture.ts is now the single implementation for BOTH capture sites - waits for each seek to genuinely settle (8s budget), confirms position + readyState, waits for a real paint (requestVideoFrameCallback with double-rAF fallback), then draws; a timed-out seek SKIPS its frame instead of recording a stale one; uniform frames dropped; runs yielding fewer than MIN_USABLE_FRAMES=4 are discarded rather than stored (a thin/black preview looks captured so nothing retried it); per-run counts logged (usable/timedOut/blank/tainted). NOTE: src/scripts/scraper-player.ts had NEVER received the frame-paint fix applied to processor.ts in v3.6.1 - I had only patched the offscreen path - and it had separately been raised to 30 segments which made the stalling worse; both now share the same 10-frame path. 7 new tests including a fake <video> that reproduces the superseded-seek stall and the all-black capture. Verified tsc clean, vitest 41/41, build OK. User will test.
